The rift costs 599.99 and is built by a company owned by Facebook. The HTC Vive costs 799.99 and is being built in coordination with Valve.

Why or why not?
Oculus Rift or the HTC Vive?

Everyone is going to say the vive because nobody like facebook, not because they have any actual knowledge of the devices. None of us has even had hands-on time with a Vive, and I'm bettiing many don't even have hands-on time with the rift. I fail to see how anyone here can argue the technical merits or failings of the vive.

It is probable that they won't be terribly different from one another. Perhaps surprisingly, doing VR is more about GPU support and application code than anything that happens in the device.

That's also the problem with letting Facebook win that battle. There isn't space for more than one or two VR headset companies.

I own a DK2 that I use regularly. Considering the Vive and the CV1 will both run 2160*1200 at 90Hz (that's the extent of the technical information that matters, to be honest), I see no reason to take the CV1.

One might just as easily argue that there is no space at all for VR at the moment because of the prohibitive cost of not only the headset, but of the equipment required to use the headset. I also own a DK2, and I don't think whitepaper specs are a good way to base a decision. We've seen before with other devices that sometimes the specs that get advertised are not always indicative of the quality of the experience.

The only way you're going to know for sure is with a solid hands-on comparison. Even for those few who can afford the price gouging Vive, I don't see the idea of "roomspace" taking off because people often don't have room to do that sort of thing properly, and the experience is tethered which means you're going to have fun tripping over wires, or worse - accidentally yanking them out of your PC. I'd point to the first iteration of the Kinnect as an example of something which required more room than the majority of people had. Despite it's other problems this was almost always the first showstopper for people.

The issue here is thinking that "not facebook" is a good thing to base your decision on. It isn't. It's stupid backwards thinking that is using something largely unimportant to color your decision. The most common fears I hear from people are that facebook will somehow make it full of ads, or use it to spy on you. This is unsubstantiated irrational crazy talk and it blows my mind that anyone could even take it seriously.

Well, my issue with CV1 is more that Oculus are absolutely 100% sellouts that took donations over false promises to stay independent. As for who they sold to, it doesn't really matter that it is Facebook specifically, more that it's the equivalent of selling a revolutionary electric engine design to a ketchup company. Any big corporation unrelated to games would be bad. But really and I can't stress that enough, it's the fact that they sold at all that disgusts me. At least by selling to Facebook and not to Microsoft or Apple there's a chance that the ecosystem will remain open and inter-operable. Yet it seems pretty much a given now that the Oculus will take part in Facebook's strategy in some way if it is at all successful. Having customers for one of the things you sell (or give out for free) is an asset, every company wants to get these customers to buy the other things too.

Now the technical part. I don't believe there's much to talk about except pixel density and framerate. Head tracking in the DK2 is pretty much as accurate as I need it to be already. I suppose it's possible to mess up the lenses and the headset geometry but that would be really, exceptionally dumb. If you make a device that needs less GPU power then good for you, but the gaming rigs required are high end regardless. And even if the spared power lets you add a lot of graphics-intensive effects, it won't matter if the pixel density doesn't allow the user to see them.
